answer: A farm running 40 keys hence forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. Because the marble stake is held until the pigment settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the jetty audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 10% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
